title: The 35 abwāb of Matn al-Bināʾ
collation: First transcribed on 2026-11-15 from a typed reading copy (takw.in, pp. 2-15), then collated entry by entry on 2026-11-16 against the page images of the printed edition listed under source 'bina' (Majmūʿ muhimmāt al-mutūn, 4th printing, Cairo 1369/1949, pp. 557-568). All 35 patterns, model verbs, maṣdars, statements of use and examples agree with the print, except: the print confirms افعيلالا for bāb 18 (the reading copy has a slip), and it writes the maṣdar of bāb 7 with hamza. Page references are to the printed edition; group labels use the wording of the text. Western equivalents were checked on 2026-11-16 against the page images of Wright vol. I (§35, §§66-72). Spelling is normalised as described in docs/data-model.md §4 (no case endings on maṣdars, hamzat al-waṣl written اِ, no sukūn on long vowels). Examples: vowel marks kept on the verb only. The first six abwāb give no maṣdar because the text gives none. Statuses are still draft: the charter defines the higher statuses for verb entries, and what they mean for a reference table is an open decision (O-10).

condition.value: The second or third radical must be one of the six guttural letters (ح خ ع غ ه ء).

abwab.note: The printed edition has the maṣdar with hamza (إفعالا، إكراما); the typed reading copy prints a plain alif.

bina.en: For plurality or intensity of the action, in the verb, the agent or the object.

ar.value: للمشاركة بين الاثنين غالباً وقد يكون للواحد

bina.en: Mostly for an action shared between two; sometimes of one agent only.
For muṭāwaʿa: the effect of a transitive action taking place.
Intensive of an intransitive; some say: for colours and defects.
For takalluf: obtaining something step by step, with effort.
For an action shared between two or more.

abwab.note: The text adds: وقيل لطلب الفعل (some say: for requesting the action), with the example استغفر الله.

masdar.note: The printed edition has افعيلالا (p. 563). The typed reading copy prints افعيعالا here, a slip that repeats the pattern of bāb 16.

western.note: The pattern اِفْعَنْلَى is Wright's Form XV; his examples there are other verbs.
Wright prints اِسْلَنْقَى itself as an example of the third quadriliteral Form, i.e. he derives it from the quadriliteral سَلْقَى, where the Matn treats it as mulḥaq of the triliteral سلق.
